How do I keep my sourdough starter alive while on holiday?

anna_bakes 14 Sep 2026

I am going away for three weeks and nobody can feed my starter. It is a 100% hydration rye starter, about two years old. What is the safest way to keep it alive until I get back?

Reply Quote Share
marco 14 Sep 2026

Feed it, let it rise for an hour, then put it in the fridge in a jar with a loose lid. A healthy rye starter survives three weeks in the fridge without trouble, it just needs two or three feeds at room temperature when you are back.

Reply Quote Share
kim_k 15 Sep 2026

Another option is to dry it: spread a thin layer on baking paper, let it dry completely for a couple of days, then crumble it and store it in an airtight jar. Dried starter keeps for months and revives in about a week of feeding.

Make a dried backup even if you use the fridge, just in case.
